items: Covers important types of Non-Verbal Reasoning frequently asked in SSC exams.
Outlines a step-by-step general method to efficiently solve non-verbal questions.
Includes comprehensive SBI-level practice questions for advanced Mixed Reasoning.
Provides complete solved examples and an answer key for thorough self-assessment.

Concept:

Non-verbal reasoning is based on figures, shapes, diagrams and visual patterns. It tests observation skills, visualisation ability and logical thinking rather than language or calculation.

Nature of Non-Verbal Questions in SSC:

• Questions are simple and direct

• Mostly observation based

• No lengthy or confusing puzzles

• Easy scoring if basic rules are clear

blocks.content: General Method to Solve Non-Verbal Questions

Step 1: Observe the basic shape of the figure.

Step 2: Count number of sides, corners, lines or dots.

Step 3: Check for symmetry, rotation or mirror image.

Step 4: Identify the pattern or rule.

Step 5: Eliminate incorrect options and select the correct one.

Example 1 (Figure Analogy):

Triangle : Square :: Square : ?



Explanation:

Triangle has 3 sides.

Square has 4 sides.

The pattern shows an increase of one side.

Therefore, Square will change to a figure having 5 sides.



Answer: Pentagon

Example 2 (Mirror Image Concept):

In mirror image questions:

• Left side becomes right

• Right side becomes left

• Top and bottom positions remain unchanged



The option showing exact left-right reversal of the figure is the correct answer.

Concept:

Mixed reasoning questions combine classification, coding-decoding, number logic and common-sense reasoning. These questions test overall logical clarity.

Nature of Mixed Reasoning Questions in SSC:

• GUIDE and direct

• One-step logic based

• No confusing or misleading statements

• Easy to moderate difficulty
Non-Verbal Reasoning question types carry high weightage in SSC competitive exams.
Mixed Reasoning sets require solving efficiency tuned to advanced SBI-level difficulty.
Understanding the General Method to Solve Non-Verbal Questions is crucial to avoiding accuracy errors under timed conditions.
